_title: Gap length versus junction specificity for NR4A3 fusion-junction gapmers: 5-6-5, 5-8-5 and 5-10-5 at the same seams
_cost: $0 — CPU only, offline over committed artifacts. No network, no credentials, no GPU and no rental.
_what: What a longer RNase-H1 catalytic gap costs and buys, measured at the SAME frame-compatible junctions the 16-mer panel was screened at, on the same instruments, with the two directions of the trade kept apart.
_why: The screened design space was 5-6-5 only, at a gap length the manuscript's own Methods place at the short end of the usable range and below the reported optimum, retained because it is what admits junction-spanning registers in a 16-mer. The manuscript concedes that nothing in it bounds what a longer gap would achieve at the same seams. This is that bound.
_what_this_is_not: Not a cleavage measurement. No RNase-H1 assay exists in this repository. Every threshold here is a REPORTED MINIMUM from retrieved literature applied to a predicted duplex, and a duplex is necessary for cleavage without being sufficient.
Not a potency, knockdown, delivery, tolerability, safety, therapeutic-window or clinical-readiness claim. No such quantity is computed anywhere in this file.
Not a recommendation of a longer gap, and not of a shorter one. It measures a trade in which one quantity improves and another worsens, and reports both.

Not a claim about which junctions patients carry. The seams here are frame-compatible, which is an arithmetic property of exon structure; breakpoint recurrence is a clinical observation and is not decided here.

Not a like-for-like transcriptome comparison unless the screens say so. The alignment arm admits a fixed TWO mismatches at every length, which is a looser FRACTIONAL threshold at 16 (14/16) than at 20 (18/20), so a lower near-match count at the longer geometry is partly that threshold and not only the sequence. The exhaustive arm is fixed at <=1 mismatch and carries the same asymmetry.

min_contiguous_dna_nt_for_rnaseh1._why_two: The retrieved sources disagree by one nucleotide and the choice would decide the headline, so both are carried and neither is presented as the answer.

5.fragment: requires a gap size of at least five for cleavage to occur
5.title: Allele-Selective Thiomorpholino Antisense Oligonucleotides as a Therapeutic Approach for Fused-in-Sarcoma Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.

6.fragment: sufficient to activate RNase H. In general, this is six or more bases
6.title: Transient Cyclic Structured Oligonucleotide Designs for Therapeutic Applications.

geometries.role: baseline — the panel the manuscript reports

mature_parent_whole_gap_duplex._threshold_note: MIN_DUPLEX_BP is an ABSOLUTE hybrid length and does not scale with the gap, so these two counts converge as the gap grows: at a gap of 10 the catalytic gap alone is already a 10 bp hybrid and every gap-pairing window clears the threshold by construction. Read the first count for how often a parent can pair the whole gap at all, and the second for how often that duplex is long enough to be a plausible substrate.

Read the first count for how often a parent can pair the whole gap at all, and the second for how often that duplex is long enough to be a plausible substrate.

the_trade._the_identity: Inside the catalytic gap the junction-unique bases on the shorter side and the bases one wild-type parent pairs on the longer side are COMPLEMENTS: they sum to the gap, which this module asserts per design rather than assuming. ⛔ THEY THEREFORE MOVE INVERSELY WITHIN A GEOMETRY, NOT TOGETHER: at a fixed gap each nucleotide of gap-level margin is one FEWER nucleotide of contiguous parent-paired DNA, and a design centred on its seam has them equal. What the identity forbids is raising the margin past the geometry's ceiling of half its gap, rounded down; that takes a longer gap, and a longer gap raises the parent-paired run at every register. ⚠ Superseded, retained (round 5, 2026-08-15): 'the gap-level margin and the contiguous parent-paired DNA rise together, nucleotide for nucleotide' — true across geometries, backwards within one, and contradicted by this module's own `parent_dna = max(gl, gr)  # = gap - margin`.

improves_with_a_longer_gap._why: A wild-type parent must match the whole gap to be a cleavable off-target there, so a longer gap is a longer coincidence to require.

junction_unique_fraction_of_the_whole_du._what: min(donor, acceptor) / length — the share of the duplex no single wild-type parent pairs. The quantity a longer oligonucleotide is expected to erode, and it erodes only at the edges of the register set: a CENTRED design sits at 0.5 whatever the length, while the most off-centre register is pinned at (wing + 1) / length and so falls from 6/16 to 6/20 as the oligonucleotide grows.

worsens_with_a_longer_gap._why: A junction-spanning design gives each parent a contiguous run of its own sequence: one LNA wing plus that parent's share of the gap. Lengthening the gap lengthens that share. The parent duplex therefore becomes both longer and more stable, and the DNA inside it approaches the run RNase-H1 needs — so the enzyme is being made more competent against the fusion and against the wild-type transcript at the same time.

the_trade._never_collapse_these: No composite score is emitted and none should be derived. A rank that mixes them would move with whichever end the weighting favours, and the finding is that they point in opposite directions.

transcriptome_coincidence_falls_but_it_M._the_bound: ⛔ At a FIXED ABSOLUTE mismatch budget a longer probe is necessarily at least as specific, and this is arithmetic rather than a result. Both arms hold the budget fixed — the alignment screen at two mismatches (>=14/16, >=16/18, >=18/20) and the exhaustive scan at one — so if an 18-mer matches a locus within the budget then every 16-mer window inside it matches within the same budget. The set of loci a longer design can hit is therefore a SUBSET of the set its own centre can hit. A falling near-match count is what the instrument guarantees; only the SIZE of the fall, and which designs reach zero, are measurements.
transcriptome_coincidence_falls_but_it_M._and_the_threshold_is_fractionally_stric: Two mismatches is 12.5 % of a 16-mer and 10.0 % of a 20-mer, so the longer geometry is also being asked a slightly stricter question. Both effects push the same way, which is why no cleanliness claim here rests on the counts alone.
transcriptome_coincidence_falls_but_it_M._and_the_denominators_differ: ⛔ THE GEOMETRIES ARE NOT SCREENED AT THE SAME NUMBER OF JUNCTIONS. The 5-6-5 panel is screened at all 38; a longer geometry is screened only where a dispatch has run. Comparing corpus totals across them would be comparing coverage, not specificity — so `matched_junctions` below restricts every geometry to the seams ALL of them were screened at, and the per-geometry block is reported for completeness rather than for comparison.

the_trade._and_ddg_is_not_selectivity: The fusion-versus-parent ΔΔG widens with length, because the fusion duplex gains from the whole added window while each parent gains only from its own side. That is not a selectivity gain in the sense that matters: what decides whether a wild-type transcript is cleaved is whether ITS duplex forms and is a substrate, not whether it is weaker than the fusion's. The absolute parent ΔG is the decision-relevant column and it moves the wrong way.

not_measured_at_the_longer_geometries._why_this_block_exists: A compartment that was screened at 5-6-5 and not at 5-8-5 or 5-10-5 must be visible as UNSCREENED. A missing arm and a clean arm are the same shape in a summary table, and the missing one is the flattering one.

exhaustive_grch38_genome_scan.state: UNAVAILABLE BY CONSTRUCTION at 18 and 20 nt, not merely unrun
exhaustive_grch38_genome_scan.why: aso_genome_offtarget is a complete 2-bit-packed bitmap over the whole 4**16 code space of a 16-mer. At 20 nt that bitmap is 4**20/8 bytes and the rolling code no longer fits the uint32 the kernel is verified over, so the module refuses by name rather than degrading. A longer window needs a different data structure, which is a build and not a parameter.
exhaustive_grch38_genome_scan.what_can_still_be_said_without_it: A BOUND, not a measurement, and it is not computed here: at a fixed absolute mismatch budget every genomic site a longer design can hit is also hit by each of its own 16-mer sub-windows, so the longer design's genome liability cannot exceed what the existing 16-mer machinery would report for any sub-window. Nobody has run that, so it is stated as an available next step and not as a result.

not_measured_at_the_longer_geometries.wet_lab: Everything. No RNase-H1 cleavage, no knockdown, no parental sparing, no delivery and no tolerability has been measured for any sequence at any geometry, here or anywhere in this repository.
not_measured_at_the_longer_geometries.lna_parameters: No LNA nearest-neighbour parameters exist in this lane, so every ΔG here is the duplex the DNA backbone would form. The wing is five nucleotides at every geometry compared, so LNA affinity enters each parent duplex identically and cannot explain a difference between them — but the absolute values are not the modified molecule's.

lead_reagent_at_the_most_commonly_report._why_this_one: EWSR1 exon 12 joined to NR4A3 exon 3 is the junction reported most often in EMC, and the 16-mer this panel ranks first at that seam also spans the TAF15 exon 11 and FUS exon 10 seams exactly. It is the one candidate in the panel with a clinical readership, so whether a longer gap leaves it cleaner or dirtier is the single most decision-relevant row here.
lead_reagent_at_the_most_commonly_report._what_is_NOT_claimed: Not that one reagent serves three patient groups. The published exon-resolved TAF15::NR4A3 breakpoints are exon 6, not exon 11, and no exon-resolved FUS::NR4A3 breakpoint has been published at all — so the three-partner property is a statement about FET-family sequence architecture at seams that may not occur.
